subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should browser private-network access grow a staged allow/block/confirm policy, and what non-overridable metadata and approval semantics should it enforce?
rationale: The request changes a security boundary and public config/CLI surface; current code has no approval contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve staged policy
options.body: Start with a narrow allow/block policy plus hard metadata/link-local behavior, then add interactive confirmation after the security contract is tested.

options.title: Approve full confirmation
options.body: Define the complete prompt UX, timeout, rate-limit, audit, redirect, and DNS-rebinding semantics before implementation begins.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Leave strict default, hostname exceptions, and broad trusted-environment opt-in as the supported browser SSRF policy for now.

recommendation.title: Approve staged policy
recommendation.body: Start with a narrow allow/block policy plus hard metadata/link-local behavior, then add interactive confirmation after the security contract is tested.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged history in the browser SSRF navigation surfaces most likely to carry the design.
